title: Stream-aggregator window collapse caused intermittent tail latency and unfair slot allocation
creator: Ava Chen
description: After a capacity burst on March 2nd, the stream-aggregator component entered repeated short-lived window collapses which produced long-tail token latencies and uneven slot allocation across customer queues. The service stayed available but several latency-sensitive customers experienced spikes above SLO for 2 hours while the cascade recovered. This ticket tracks the follow-ups, permanent mitigations, and verification work for the incident.
impact_summary: Duration: intermittent spikes between 03:12 and 05:20 UTC on 2026-03-02
Scope: small percentage of requests (~0.6% of incoming QPS) but high amplification of tail latency for affected customers
Symptoms: in telemetry we saw sudden drop in average aggregation window depth, followed by a surge in per-slot occupancy and increased variance in token latencies
Customer visible: increased 95/99th token latency for hosted API routes using long-context models; no data loss or incorrect outputs
root_cause: Regression introduced in adaptive-window tuning (runtime-1.18) made the aggregator shrink windows too aggressively when input patterns had high short-burst variance
Shrink events were not properly gated by recent slot-occupancy history, allowing a rapid sequence of collapses under bursty tail workloads
Slot allocation logic lacked a cap on consecutive acquisitions by a single producer, enabling priority inversion/favoring for certain request lanes
short_term_mitigations: Rollback adaptive-window delta from runtime-1.18 -> rolled back at 03:35 UTC (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8612)
Apply emergency guard: minimum window floor of 8 tokens for 24 hours (config flag enabled via feature-flags)
Throttle aggressive producers via temporary rate-shaping at edge to limit burst amplification (edge rule ID: edge-rule-2026-03-02-09)
permanent_action_items: Implement slot-occupancy EWMA and require stable occupancy < threshold before allowing window shrink (owner: Marco Rivera, estimate: 5)
Add consecutive-acquisition cap to slot allocator to prevent single-lane dominance; ensure fairness across customer lanes (owner: Priya Patel, estimate: 3)
Instrument and emit 'window-collapse' event metric with tags (model_family, customer_id, region) and a histogram of pre/post window depths (owner: Ethan Kim, estimate: 3)
Create regression test harness (LoadReplay) with bursty traffic profiles and validate adaptive-window behavior in CI (owner: Laura Gomez, estimate: 5)
Introduce canary sweep for adaptive-window changes that runs in production on 5% of traffic and auto-reverts on >5% tail-latency regression (owner: Marco Rivera, estimate: 8)
Update runbook: include steps to identify window-collapse via new metrics, and ordered mitigations (owner: Ava Chen, estimate: 2)
acceptance_criteria: Window-occupancy metric shows fewer than 1 collapse per 10M requests on LoadReplay burst profile
No tail-latency regression (>5% increase in p99 tokens) observed on canary during 72h of continuous burst testing
Post-deploy dashboard shows fair slot distribution across customer lanes for 48h after rollout
Runbook verified by on-call and SRE during one fire-drill and updated in Confluence (link below)
verification_plan: Run LoadReplay scenario 'burst-10x-short' nightly for 7 days against canary cluster and collect window-collapse events
Synthetic customers: run per-tenant fairness synthetic that asserts max consecutive slot acquisitions < 4
Dashboard alerts: create alert for 'window-collapse rate > 0.5/min' and 'slot-occupancy variance increase > 2x'
Post-merge: schedule 24h smoke with SE/CS for affected customers to confirm latency improvement
notes: This incident is distinct from previous coalescer-freeze incidents: root cause is tuning regression in adaptive-window heuristics rather than a lock or timer drift
We should consider adding a canary-only 'non-shrinking' mode to facilitate safer tuning iterations
Edge rate-shaping created backpressure that highlighted downstream fairness issues; long-term solution must live in aggregator to avoid customer-visible throttles
